agree.reason: The plain, respectful account and seniority shift choice will keep many staff open to it, but a long-tenured teller who dreads phone work gets no reason to try it, because the 6-month severance safety net and the $1.50 raise are both missing.

honest.reason: It drops the unsupported 'better for everyone' claim and states the schedule frankly, though the line that start and training dates are not yet set is not in the brief and may be invented.

works_the_facts.reason: It repeats the raw figures but leaves 'same pay or higher' where the true, stronger '$1.50 an hour more' was available, and it never turns the severance into a concrete figure, such as 20 weeks' pay for ten years of service.

right_comparison.reason: It sets falling branch visits (44% down) against rising phone and chat demand (60% up) and the 9-minute hold time as the cost of standing still, and it puts severance plainly as the staff member's alternative.

qualification.reason: Offers by Feb 14 and decisions by Mar 1 are dated and checkable, but the open-ended 'we'll share start dates as soon as they're decided' gives no date, and the safety net of leaving within 6 months is left out.

objections.reason: It deals head-on with the loss of 9-to-5 hours by offering seniority-based shift choice, but it never addresses the main objection, not wanting phone work, even though the 6-month opt-out with severance answers it directly.

fit.reason: It is a COO email of about 420 words, close to the length asked for, but the signature has no name and the credit union is never named.
